title: Balancing Northern Metropolis development opportunities with housing pressure and career pathways for Hong Kong diploma graduates
topic_description: Government and industry promote the Northern Metropolis as an innovation and career hub, but young people worry about housing timelines, cross-boundary commuting, and whether diploma pathways truly align with hiring reality. Your group includes student leaders and a youth council observer. Discuss how schools should prepare Form 4–6 students, what role JUPAS vs GBA articulation should play, and how to evaluate marketing claims critically.
instructions: You have 1 minute to prepare and 8 minutes for the group discussion (10 minutes for a group of 4). You should interact with your fellow candidates. Do not read out prepared notes. You may make notes during the preparation time, but you should not write out everything you plan to say.
discussion_points: How careers education should combine skills mapping with realistic information about housing supply and commute costs.
Equity: students without resources to travel or rent near new hubs—alternative pathways and dignity.
Critical literacy toward mega-project messaging—what counts as evidence (occupancy dates, offer letters, labour conditions).
individual_response_questions: Should the government legally require developers to publish occupancy timelines alongside promotional materials?
How can English and LS curricula ethically integrate GBA case studies without pressuring students toward a single identity outcome?
hkeaa_alignment: Paper 4: communication of ideas, discourse management, language resources for abstract topics; intelligibility.
success_feedback: You sustained abstract policy–personal discussion appropriately.
suggested_next_steps: Debate club: timed rebuttal on one statistic from the talk.
Shadow a careers counsellor’s opening question list.
